A settings-aware wrapper for the SW (pattern list cached via watchSettings so the hot path stays synchronous)
Enforcement at all three real chokepoints: commands.ts:93 activateTool, commands.ts:168 activateResume, capture-service.ts:79 assertShootable
Honest popup state: src/pages/popup/context.ts:86 must surface the new reason so the UI says 'excluded', not 'restricted'

naturalSplitPoints.whyThisBoundary: Rasd_Plan.md:1327-1333 and ADR 0013 section 4 both pull this OUT of phase 20 as a standalone item that ships BEFORE the MVP gate and does not wait for the rest of 20. It is also the only part of 20 that touches the background/content boundary rather than pages/ - different blast radius, different reviewers - and it can land while 19 is still in flight. It must NOT be bundled with the management UI: the plan says explicitly «الإنفاذ من طبقة الحقن لا من الواجهة».

naturalSplitPoints.whyThisBoundary: These four tabs are homogeneous form work against keys that already exist in schema.ts - Toggle/Radio/Slider/SegmentedControl/Input are all built. planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «البوّابة الوحيدة للحقن. كل مسار يريد تشغيل شيء داخل صفحة يمرّ من هنا.» - and ADR 0005's «ويمرّ من بوّابة واحدة».
planClaimsRefutedByCode.claimLocation: src/background/index.ts:34-37 (doc comment over canOperateOnTab); Docs/ADR/0005-manual-injection.md under «القرار»; echoed by Rasd_Plan.md:1329 «والبوابة الواحدة قائمة — فالعمل صغير».
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: canOperateOnTab - the function that doc comment sits on - has ZERO callers anywhere. The predicate checkInjectable is instead called independently at seven sites. The real chokepoint for injection is commands.ts (two functions), and there is a SECOND, separate chokepoint for capture (assertShootable in capture-service.ts) that no path through commands.ts covers. So the pre-MVP excludedSites work touches at least three functions, not one.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: `grep -rn 'canOperateOnTab' src/ tests/ scripts/` -> exactly one hit, the definition at src/background/index.ts:39. `grep -rn 'checkInjectable|isInjectable' src/` -> call sites at background/commands.ts:95, background/commands.ts:170, background/capture-service.ts:91, background/lifecycle.ts:110, background/index.ts:40, background/resume.ts:24, pages/popup/context.ts:86. `grep -rn 'executeScript' src/` -> only commands.ts:66, :98, :172.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: The message 'tab/can-operate' exists as the way other contexts ask the single gate whether a tab is operable.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: The handler is registered but nothing in src/ ever sends 'tab/can-operate'. The popup deliberately bypasses it and calls checkInjectable locally, which its own docstring states as the non-obvious decision of that file. Any excludedSites check added only to that handler would therefore reach nobody.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: `grep -rn 'tab/can-operate' src/ tests/ scripts/` -> contract.ts:85, contract.ts:341, lifecycle.ts:108 (handler), and pages/popup/context.ts:6, which is a comment explaining the bypass. No send() call exists. popup/context.ts:5 reads «القرار الوحيد غير البديهي هنا: `checkInjectable(url)` يُستدعى محليًّا لا عبر...»

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: ADR 0005's flow diagram: «إيماءة -> activeTab يُمنح -> checkInjectable(url) -> executeScript», i.e. every injection follows an explicit user gesture.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: activateResume() injects content.js with NO user gesture, fired from a chrome.tabs.onUpdated listener and gated on an optional host permission instead. The ADR's closing bullet acknowledges host permissions for persistence, but the stated gate flow does not, and commands.ts:154-158 documents the exception explicitly. This matters for excludedSites: the automatic path needs the same check and is the easiest one to overlook.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: src/background/resume.ts:21-30 (chrome.tabs.onUpdated -> activateResume, guarded only by checkInjectable + chrome.permissions.contains); src/background/commands.ts:154-158 «يستأنف وضع المقارنة تلقائيًّا بعد تنقّل — **بلا إيماءة مستخدم**»; injection at commands.ts:172.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: «`onChanged` يبثّ إلى كل السياقات (النافذة، الصفحات، الـservice worker، الطبقة داخل الصفحة) بلا رسائل يدوية.»
planClaimsRefutedByCode.reality: True of the Chrome API, false of this codebase. The chrome.storage.onChanged listener is installed only by ensureWatcher(), which runs only from watchSettings(), which has no production caller. So today no production context receives the broadcast, and getSettings()'s module-level cache (line 16, set at line 28) is never invalidated in any context that did not call watchSettings. Phase 20's integration test «ينعكس فورًا في كل السياقات» will fail against the current wiring.
planClaimsRefutedByCode.evidence: src/shared/settings/index.ts:60-76 (watchSettings -> ensureWatcher -> addListener). `grep -rn 'watchSettings|ensureWatcher' src/ tests/` -> production hits: none; test hits only at tests/unit/settings.test.ts:105 and :112. Consumers read once instead: src/content/index.ts:219 `void getSettings().then(...)`.

planClaimsRefutedByCode.claim: Phase 20 ships «إعدادات المظهر: الوضع الداكن/الفاتح/النظام، اللغة (عربي افتراضي / إنجليزي)، الكثافة» as settings-screen work.

openQuestions: Should excludedSites be enforced by extending checkInjectable (which would make it async or require passing the pattern list in, rippling to all 7 call sites) or by a separate settings-aware gate that wraps it? The pure/sync property of checkInjectable is load-bearing for tests/unit/restricted.test.ts and for the popup, which calls it locally rather than over a message.

What are the exact excludedSites pattern semantics? The schema is `string[]` with no syntax. Decide and write down: does a bare `bank.com` match subdomains? Is `*.bank.com` inclusive of the apex? Are path patterns supported (section 11.2 mentions admin panels, which are often path-scoped)? How are ports, punycode/IDN, uppercase hosts and trailing-dot FQDNs normalised? The whole security value of this item sits in these answers.

Does the plan intend excludedSites to block CAPTURE as well as injection? capture-service.ts's assertShootable is a separate chokepoint on chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab. A user who excludes their bank almost certainly means 'never screenshot it either', but the plan's wording is «لا يقبل الحقن أصلًا» (does not accept injection).

shared/permissions.ts revokePermission returns 'granted' when chrome.permissions.remove succeeds (permissions.ts:69-70), and this is locked in by tests/unit/permissions.test.ts:96. The permissions screen's revoke button will read as `outcome === 'granted'` meaning 'successfully revoked'. Is this deliberate naming that should stay, or should the outcome type gain a 'revoked' member before a UI depends on it?

Rasd_Plan.md section 3.5 (the unified bilingual acceptance criterion: numeral policy, bidi isolation, RTL mirroring rules) states it applies to «مراحل الواجهة (12-19)». Phase 20 produces nine UI screens but falls outside that stated range. Is this an intentional exemption or a range that should read 12-20? The settings screens are full of technical values (hex, px, 1440x900, key caps) that section 3.5 governs directly.

settings.schemaVersion is pinned at 1 (schema.ts:35) and nothing in the repo reads it. Phase 20 adds keys (shortcuts, saveLocation, library lock) and introduces settings import from a file. Does a migration path get defined here, and does the import path validate schemaVersion before accepting a file written by a newer build?

Should the whole-section salvage in parseSettings (schema.ts:128-137) be narrowed before settings import ships? Today one bad nested key silently discards its entire top-level section (proven by tests/unit/settings.test.ts:60-67). That is defensible for corrupt storage; it is user-hostile for a hand-edited import file.

Section 11.1 asks for two private-browsing behaviours (block auto-save, or disable the extension entirely). Does 'disable entirely' mean the injection gate refuses incognito tabs outright? If so it belongs with the 20-qabl enforcement work, not with the 20-alef-3 UI, and it needs a schema key that does not exist.

What is the honest threat model for the library lock, and who decides it? A passcode over the UI does not protect IndexedDB from devtools or from another extension with storage access. The acceptance criterion «يمنع القراءة قبل فتح القفل» can mean 'the UI refuses to read' or 'the data at rest is encrypted' - these differ by an order of magnitude in size and in what may be claimed to users.

Is a Modal/Dialog component expected as part of phase 20, or should delete-all-data and unlock reuse the documented window.confirm precedent from the library (SelectionBar.tsx:67-69)? The component library is declared complete at 20 components in src/ui/components/index.ts, so adding one is a design-system change, not just a page detail.

Phase 19 has not started, and stripMetadataOnExport has no meaning without the export pipeline. Should the privacy screen ship that toggle disabled with a 'coming' marker (the pattern phase 21 uses for cloud share links), or should the toggle be withheld until 19 lands?

Section 6 item 56 records a double-injection bug in src/content/host.ts (toPublic() opens the host but forgets layer.setAttribute, so a second activation silently kills pointer interactivity) and assigns it to «المرحلة 20 أو 22». Since 20-qabl already touches the activation path, should that one-line fix plus a double-injection test be folded into it, or explicitly left to 22?
